diagram_math_checks.evidence: Definition lines 29 and 34 fix one real or complex inner-product space and orthonormal v_1,...,v_j. A acts on that same space, so Av_j, each h_ij v_i, and w_j are vectors in it. The inner product yields a scalar h_ij and the norm yields a nonnegative real h_{j+1,j}. Diagram arrows indicate computational order, not vector-space morphisms or asserted commutative squares.

Diagram lines 64 and 66 exactly reproduce Definition lines 36 and 40, with 1 <= i <= j and column index j. The local supplier def-inner-product-space explicitly uses linearity in the first argument, so h_ij=<Av_j,v_i> is the correct coefficient. Orthonormality gives <w_j,v_k>=h_kj-sum_i h_ij delta_ik=0 for each k<=j. No conjugation or sign is changed.

Diagram line 68 reproduces line 44. By positive definiteness in def-inner-product-space and the induced norm definition, ||w_j||=0 iff w_j=0. The nonzero branch divides by h_{j+1,j} exactly as lines 46-48; its output is a unit vector orthogonal to the current vectors. The zero branch stops at step j exactly as lines 50-51 and never attempts division by zero. Both branch labels retain h_{j+1,j}, not h_{j,j+1}.

All five rendered arrows go forward: input -> coefficients -> residual -> norm, then norm -> normalized new vector or norm -> exact breakdown. This is a fixed-step recurrence schematic; it introduces no matrix dimensions or new Hessenberg identity and preserves the existing Krylov supplier interface. The coefficient rows 1,...,j and optional subdiagonal h_{j+1,j} retain the original Arnoldi indexing. No new statement, dependency or proof claim is inferred from the picture.

The complete original Definition is byte-preserved, and the Remarks explicitly say that the diagram restates it. This proof-free definition remains complete without the figure; any rigorous argument remains independent of it.
